title: Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule
summary: Distance-based stock pairs earned 1.44%/month (top 20, 1962-2002), 0.90% with a one-day delay; raw returns fell from 118 to 38 bp/month after 1988.

title: Does Simple Pairs Trading Still Work?
summary: Top-20 pairs returns fell from 0.86%/month (1962-88) to 0.37% (1989-2002) and 0.24% (2003-09), driven by non-converging pairs; largely unprofitable after costs.

title: Statistical Arbitrage Pairs Trading Strategies: Review and Outlook
summary: Review of 90+ pairs-trading papers: distance, cointegration, time-series, stochastic control; decay of GGR, commodity spreads with physical links work, gold-silver spread did not.

title: Pairs Trading in Cryptocurrency Markets
summary: Distance and cointegration pairs on crypto: profitable only in some sub-periods and weaker than older pairs literature (abstract and summaries only).

title: Statistical Arbitrage - An Easy Walkthrough (and Hacker News discussion)
summary: Avellaneda-Lee residual stat-arb on JPM/XLF lost money and ETH/BTC was barely positive; practitioners say single-pair stat-arb no longer works.

title: Gold/silver ratio near two-year high: Bank of America cointegration test
summary: BofA finds gold and silver cointegrated in only 20% of monthly windows since 1996, mostly during crises; the relationship broke in 2020.

title: The Weak Tie Between Natural Gas and Oil Prices
summary: Oil and gas were cointegrated with unstable regimes and no significant cointegration from 2009; other studies date the decoupling to the shale boom.

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
summary: Cross-sectional momentum works in small universes: 18 country index futures 8.7%/yr Sharpe 0.73, 27 commodities 12.4%/yr Sharpe 0.53 (to 2011, before costs).

title: Short-term Momentum
summary: One-month returns reverse in low-turnover stocks but continue in high-turnover, large, liquid stocks, as strongly as 12-month momentum and after costs.

title: Relative Strength Strategies for Investing
summary: Top 1-3 of 10 US sectors (1928-2009) and of 5 global asset classes (1973-2009) by trailing return beat buy-and-hold in ~70% of years by ~3-6%/yr before costs.

title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
summary: 10-month SMA timing on 5 asset classes: 1973-2012 about 10.5%/yr at 7% volatility vs 9.9% at 10.3% for buy-and-hold, drawdown under 10% vs 46% (via secondary sources).

title: Global Tactical Asset Allocation (out-of-sample extension to 2025)
summary: Extending Faber's GTAA (200-day SMA) to March 2025: out-of-sample CAGR 6.05%, Sharpe 0.68, max drawdown 11.7%.

title: Risk Premia Harvesting Through Dual Momentum
summary: Dual momentum (relative plus absolute 12-month momentum) beats either alone; Global Equity Momentum switches between US, non-US stocks and bonds monthly (1974-2011).

title: Relative and Absolute Momentum in Times of Rising/Low Yields: Bold Asset Allocation (BAA)
summary: Keller's BAA combines PAA, VAA and DAA ideas: SMA(12) relative momentum, 13612W canary (SPY, VWO, VEA, BND); claims >=20%/yr with <=15% drawdown 1970-2022 (flagged as likely overfit by Allocate Smartly).

title: Allocate Smartly: strategy selection by recent performance, equity-curve trend, distressed strategies, wisdom of 100 strategies, costs, 2022, KDA
summary: Across 100+ TAA strategies since 1973, picking recent winners by return or Sharpe never beat the equal-weighted average on Sharpe; aggregate allocation earned Sharpe 1.06 (2000-2026).

title: A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing
summary: Time-series momentum on 67 markets 1880-2013: 14.9%/yr gross, 11.2% after 2-and-20, Sharpe 0.77 net, zero correlation to stocks, positive every decade.

title: Diversification and small account size
summary: Rule-of-thumb trend/carry Sharpe rises from 0.35 with 1 instrument to 0.61 with 8 (one per asset class) and 0.70 with 37.

title: Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity
summary: Levered risk parity of US stocks and bonds 1926-2010: excess return 7.99%/yr, Sharpe 0.53 vs 0.25 for the market portfolio; broad sample 0.61 vs 0.43.

title: Building Diversified Portfolios that Outperform Out-of-Sample (Hierarchical Risk Parity)
summary: HRP clusters by correlation and allocates by inverse variance; in Monte Carlo its out-of-sample variance was 0.067 vs 0.093 inverse-variance and 0.116 minimum-variance.

title: Optimal Versus Naive Diversification: How Inefficient is the 1/N Portfolio Strategy?
authors: DeMiguel, Garlappi, Uppal (Review of Financial Studies)
summary: None of 14 optimisers consistently beat equal weights; mean-variance needs ~3000 months of data to beat 1/N with 25 assets.

title: What is return stacking; HFEA leveraged risk-parity case
summary: Return stacking puts $2 of exposure on $1 and must clear its financing cost; a 3x stock/bond portfolio lost about 71% peak to trough by 2023 when the bond hedge failed.

title: Factor Momentum and the Momentum Factor
authors: Ehsani, Linnainmaa (NBER w25551; Journal of Finance 2022)
summary: Factors earned 52-53 bp/month after a positive year vs 1-2 bp after a negative one; time-series factor momentum 4.2%/yr (t=7.0), 1964-2015.

title: Factor Momentum Everywhere
summary: 59 of 65 equity factors show positive time-series momentum; buying recent winning factors and selling losers earns significant returns, also outside the US.

title: Timing the Factor Zoo
summary: Timing 300+ factors with 39 signals: past factor returns and volatility are the strongest predictors; the median timed factor gains about 2%/yr.

title: Why and How Systematic Strategies Decay
summary: Post-publication Sharpe of anomalies is about 55% of in-sample (median); decay grows ~5 percentage points per year of publication and with signal complexity.

title: Adaptive Portfolio by Solving Multi-armed Bandit via Thompson Sampling
summary: Treats classic portfolio strategies as bandit arms selected by Thompson sampling with a risk-preference reward; backtest gains on standard datasets, no live evidence.

title: When Influence Misleads: Informational and Strategic Limits of Social Learning in Trading Networks
summary: eToro 2013 data on 164,634 traders: mirrored trades lost 61 bp vs 7 bp for own trades; trader performance autocorrelation matches a null model; copiers follow popularity.

title: Copy Trading
summary: Experiment: information on others' success raises risk taking and the copy option raises it more; 88% of copiers copied someone holding the riskiest choice.

title: Benefits from social trading? Empirical evidence for certificates on wikifolios
authors: Oehler, Horn, Wendt (International Review of Financial Analysis)
summary: 1,084 wikifolio certificates (2012-13) did not outperform on average; the best earned short-term excess returns.

title: Darwinex risk engine, investable attributes and DarwinIA allocation
summary: Darwinex rescales every strategy to 3.25-6.5% monthly VaR, scores performance against 10,000 random strategies of the same risk, requires experience, and allocates for 3-6 month terms.

title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
summary: Gives the expected maximum Sharpe among N trials (about 3.0 standard units for N=450-480) and a deflated Sharpe that corrects for selection, skew, kurtosis and length.

title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
authors: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado, Zhu
summary: CSCV method to estimate the probability that the in-sample best configuration underperforms the median out of sample.

title: Our instruments together: volatilities, correlations, spreads (2024-01 to 2026-09)
summary: Local daily data: US100-US500 corr 0.95, 8 shares mean corr 0.38 (~3.9 effective bets), all 20 instruments ~6.1 effective bets; spreads and ratio ranges.

title: Global Equity Momentum: A Craftsman's Perspective
summary: Antonacci extends GEM to 1950-2018 and treats 2012-2018 as out of sample; argues against over-optimising the lookback.
